reviewer: Codex operator — owner-authorised Phase 5H sampled editorial review
method: 65 design representatives inspected on six contact sheets; previously approved canary copy protected. Unverified Spotlight and Velour excluded from activation. No colours inferred from names and no performance claims.

designs.visualDescription: Overlapping pointed leaves create a flowing botanical pattern, with fine lines adding a woven, layered appearance.
Interlocking angular shapes form a compact geometric pattern, with stitched lines giving the surface visible depth.
Fine diagonal lines meet in angular blocks, creating a geometric pattern that changes direction across the fabric.
Closely spaced ribs give this plain fabric its visible texture, offering interest without a large patterned motif.
Fine horizontal striations give this plain fabric a gently varied surface, making it a quiet companion to patterned furnishings.
Bands of different widths form a crisp stripe, with fine accent lines adding definition between the broader bands.
Small repeated oval motifs make an orderly geometric pattern, adding close-up detail to the woven ground.
Small diamond motifs repeat across a gently mottled ground, giving the design a relaxed geometric character.
Alternating blocks of fine horizontal and vertical lines create a basket-like checked pattern with a layered woven appearance.
Repeated flower-like geometric motifs sit in a diamond arrangement, with softly broken outlines lending the print an informal character.
Stepped, interlocking lines form a bold geometric repeat, with a softly textured ground tempering the angular design.
Fine interlocking angular lines create a compact maze-like repeat. The small motif adds detail without a single dominant focal shape.
Linked oval motifs form slim vertical chains on a quieter ground. Their regular spacing gives the design an orderly rhythm.
Closely drawn lines change direction within a grid of triangles and diamonds. The shifting angles give this woven geometric a layered appearance.
Small alternating blocks form an even checkerboard pattern. Subtle changes within the squares soften the rigid grid.
Short groups of horizontal and vertical strokes form open rectangular blocks. The supplier identifies this as a sheer fabric, suited to a lighter layered curtain treatment.
A low-contrast diamond lattice sits across the textured ground. The restrained repeat keeps the overall effect quieter than a strongly outlined pattern.
Fine broken vertical lines and small linked shapes create an irregular stripe. The supplier identifies this as a sheer, offering another layer alongside the main curtains.
Repeated triangular segments meet in small pinwheel-like forms. The crisp tessellation gives the design a lively, evenly distributed pattern.
Tiny evenly spaced dots punctuate an otherwise quiet ground. This restrained repeat can add detail beside larger patterns elsewhere in the room.
Loose wavy lines travel vertically across the fabric, crossing and separating like fine branches. Their irregular paths soften the strong direction of the design.
Fine horizontal striations give this near-plain fabric a subtle layered appearance. It offers visual texture without a prominent pictorial motif.
Small linked bar-and-dot motifs are spaced evenly across a quiet ground. The open arrangement makes the pattern feel less dense than an all-over lattice.
Tiny repeated marks sit in a regular grid across a pale-looking ground. The supplier identifies this as a sheer fabric for a lighter curtain layer.
Narrow irregular bars overlap in a layered rectangular pattern. The supplier identifies the fabric as velvet, adding a different surface character to the graphic design.
Clouded, irregular patches merge into an all-over abstract print. The edges are soft and varied rather than arranged in a rigid grid.
Closely spaced undulating lines form a continuous wave pattern. The repeated curves give the fabric movement without a large isolated motif.
Broad broken zigzags combine irregular edges with smaller contrasting marks. The supplier identifies this as velvet, pairing a graphic pattern with a pile surface.
An irregular linked trellis forms repeating pointed oval shapes. The supplier identifies this as velvet; the open lattice gives it a clear decorative rhythm.
Repeated chevrons have uneven, painterly edges rather than perfectly straight lines. The layered bands create a strong directional pattern.
A fine low-contrast diagonal lattice lies across a near-plain ground. The detail becomes more apparent at close range, making it a restrained geometric option.
Many small elongated marks form softly swirling clusters across the surface. The changing directions create an organic all-over texture.
Irregular oval and diamond-like motifs repeat in offset rows. Their blurred edges give the pattern an expressive, painterly quality.
Fine irregular strokes gather into repeated chevron bands. The supplier identifies the fabric as velvet, combining visible pile with a directional design.
Long uneven vertical marks overlap to form a loose stripe. Variations in thickness break up the regularity and give the surface a layered appearance.
Small stylised flower sprigs repeat in neat rows with generous space between them. The compact motif brings a gentle decorative accent to the curtains.
Small rounded motifs join into a dense, regular geometric repeat. The closely spaced pattern provides detail across the whole fabric rather than one large focal motif.
Slender diagonal lines cross to create an open diamond trellis. Small variations along the lines give the lattice a stitched appearance.
Upright stems with paired leaves form repeated vertical bands. The simple stylised foliage combines a botanical motif with the order of a stripe.
Very small repeated checks form a tightly spaced grid. The compact scale makes the pattern read more quietly from a distance.
Fine curling stems, leaves and small flower-like marks fill the ground. The scattered arrangement creates an informal garden-inspired pattern.
Small leaf sprigs are scattered in changing directions across the ground. Their loose arrangement creates a lively all-over foliage print.
Nested angular lines form a repeated diamond and chevron pattern. The fine broken strokes add detail within the larger geometric structure.
Small rounded flower-like marks sit in an evenly spaced repeat. The modest scale creates a gentle decorative pattern across the fabric.
Alternating slim and broader vertical bands form a balanced stripe. Fine lines within the bands add another level of detail.
A compact linked lattice makes an even all-over repeat. The small open shapes give the print a tidy, regular character.
Decorative medallions and small floral motifs form a dense ornamental print. The varied shapes make this a useful focal fabric beside simpler finishes.
Broad crossing bands and finer companion lines create a traditional plaid. The clear grid gives the fabric a structured, familiar pattern.
Layered oval medallions repeat in close rows, with smaller shapes nested inside each motif. The busy ornamental print makes a distinct decorative statement.
Large stylised floral medallions connect through curling stems and smaller leaves. The open ornamental arrangement gives each motif room to stand out.
Alternating vertical bands are separated by groups of fine lines. The regular stripe offers a clear sense of direction across the curtain fabric.
Dense stylised leaves and small floral forms create a compact all-over print. The repeated foliage provides a decorative layer without one dominant flower.
Small stylised leaf motifs sit in orderly offset rows. The generous ground between them keeps this ornamental repeat relatively open.
Loose flowers, leaves and curling stems spread across the ground in varied directions. The open garden-inspired composition gives the print an informal character.
Broken horizontal streaks create a strongly striated near-plain surface. The irregular marks add visual depth without a recognisable floral or geometric motif.
Parallel bands of varying widths run across the supplier image. Confirm the stripe direction when planning the curtain layout and fabric cutting.
Broad vertical bands are bordered by fine paired lines. The clear spacing produces a calm, traditional striped arrangement.
Closely repeated rounded arches contain small nested details. The dense scalloped rhythm gives this geometric fabric an ornamental character.
Groups of fine vertical lines alternate with wider bands. The change in line weight adds detail to an otherwise regular stripe.
Many narrow vertical lines repeat at close intervals. The fine spacing creates a more detailed striped surface than a broad block stripe.
Slim line groups and wider vertical bands alternate in a measured rhythm. The variation in stripe width gives the design a balanced decorative structure.
Broad vertical bands alternate across a visibly woven ground. The straightforward stripe leaves room for more intricate patterns elsewhere in the room.
Fine vertical lines sit beside broader shaded bands. The contrasting widths give this woven stripe a layered but orderly appearance.
